source_subtype: professional community portal + trade news + industry conference organiser
why_relevant: Self-described largest Czech community site for financial advisers, operated by 4stones, s.r.o. (Prague, ICO 29002303), claiming ~20,000 monthly active users and ~15,000 registered members. Carries 'Aktualne z trhu' market news, video interviews and podcasts, discussion forums, and organises FINfest, a major industry conference. Covers advisory firms, insurance, investment, loans/mortgages/building savings, pensions, and explicitly regulation and distribution trends. The discussion forums are the distinctive asset: practitioner threads reveal bank commission changes, product-condition tightening and service problems well before they are written up anywhere, and the FINfest programme names who is speaking.

source_subtype: SME business portal (same publisher family as Mesec.cz)
why_relevant: Czech SME business portal (Internet Info group, sister to Mesec.cz), tagline 'cesta k vlastnimu byznysu'. Matters to this cell because the merchant/SME side of banking - business current accounts, payment terminals, acquiring, e-commerce payment obligations - is largely invisible in consumer portals and in annual reports, and this is where it is covered. Observed items included a new service consolidating company accounts held at multiple banks into one overview, and a new obligation for e-shops. Sections: /clanky/, /pribehy-podnikatelu/, /poradna/, /kalkulacky/, /zakony/, /smlouvy/, /rejstrik/, /kurzy/. Caveat: bank fees for businesses were not prominent in the sample fetched, so yield on the fee angle specifically is unproven.

Czech-language 'online magazin o fintech inovacich a trendy technologiich'. Covers Czech banks by name (Ceska sporitelna, Moneta observed), accounts and banking, mortgages, savings and investments, consumer loans, taxes and pensions, and Czech regulatory topics. Sits in the gap between the consumer fee portals and the paywalled institutional trade press: fintech-native commentary on Czech bank product and technology moves, freely accessible. Ownership/operator is not disclosed on the pages fetched, which caps how far it can be trusted on its own.

source_subtype: long-form financial magazine (subdomain of a consumer-finance portal)
why_relevant: Long-form Czech financial-journalism title published on the Penize.cz infrastructure (Partners media stable), the analytical/essayistic sister to the transactional Penize.cz comparison layer. Relevant to this cell as the place where Czech banking-sector structural arguments, executive profiles and critical takes on fee and product practice get written at length rather than as news briefs. NOT VERIFIED IN THIS RUN: returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to the fetcher, exactly as the parent domain penize.cz did - consistent with a publisher-level WAF, so the hypothesis is bot-defended-but-live, not dead.

source_subtype: large aggregator financial portal with bank fee-schedule and ATM verticals
why_relevant: Kurzy.cz bills itself as 'nejvetsi cesky financni portal' and is operated by Kurzy.cz, spol. s r.o. together with AliaWeb, spol. s r.o. Its navigation exposes dedicated verticals for banks (/banky/), bank fee schedules (/banky/sazebniky/) and ATMs (/bankomaty/), which would make it a fourth independent normalisation of Czech bank fee and ATM-network data. PARTIALLY VERIFIED ONLY: three fetches (/banky/, /banky/sazebniky/, /bankomaty/) each returned the site header, publisher identification and navigation but no section body - consistent with client-side rendering or a content gate rather than an error, since no 404 or 403 was raised. The sazebniky and bankomaty paths were observed as real navigation targets, but their contents are unconfirmed.

source_subtype: independent investment publication for investors and professionals
why_relevant: Independent Czech investment and finance publication run by MONECO, spol. s r.o. (Brno, established 1997), aimed at individual investors and financial professionals. Sections cover markets and news, facts and advice, funds and ETFs, editorial opinion and an investment academy. Marginal for the bank-fee angle but relevant to this run's 'investor relations / earnings' topic set as an independent Czech professional read on listed financial institutions and fund products distributed through bank channels. Confirmed live.

source_subtype: financial news portal owned by an FX/corporate-finance group
why_relevant: Financial-news and FX property operated by Roklen Holding a.s. (Prague), part of a group that also contains RoklenFx and Roklen Corporate Finance. Sections: Novinky, Menove pary (EUR/USD, EUR/CZK, USD/CZK, GBP/CZK), FX pruvodce, Ekonomicky kalendar. Relevant to this cell chiefly on the payments/FX-conditions edge - e.g. cross-border and e-commerce currency-conversion practice, where non-bank FX providers publish comparisons that expose bank FX margins that banks themselves never state as a headline number. Editorial mix observed skewed to FX and macro rather than retail bank fees, and its ownership by an FX provider is a direct competitive interest in how bank FX pricing is portrayed.

source_subtype: general economics/business news site with a finance desk
why_relevant: Czech news site tagged 'ekonomika, politika, byznys a finance', managed by Copywrite Company s.r.o., with sections spanning economics, politics, EU affairs, finance, business, investments, plus a podcasts/interviews section. Despite the fintech-suggestive name the observed coverage was general economic and political news (US debt, digital currencies, Czech pensions, pharma competition, Ukraine) rather than Czech retail-bank product or fee detail. Recorded here for completeness of the cell's media map and because its podcast/interview strand may carry Czech financial-sector executives, but yield for this cell's specific topics is unproven and looks thin.

A time-stamped rolling feed of short Czech business/startup/tech items, updated multiple times per day (items observed at 06:33, 07:16, 11:04 on the fetch date). This is the highest-cadence weak-signal channel on CzechCrunch: short launch/partnership/funding notices land here that never become full features. Confirmed to carry fintech items — e.g. 'Fintech Roger loni rostl o 40 procent, profinancoval faktury za téměř 13 miliard korun' and 'ČSOB a Mastercard vybraly do Fintech Challenge šest startupů', both under the /live/ path.

CzechCrunch does not appear to expose a dedicated /fintech/ tag archive (see negative findings), so on-site search is the practical entry point into its fintech back-catalogue. The query 'fintech' returned 38 results with a clean pagination pattern (https://cc.cz/page/N/?s=fintech), and the result set itself acts as an actor map: Roger, Sype.to, ČSOB, Mastercard, Fintech Week CEE, Fintech Challenge all surfaced from one query.

201-episode Czech business podcast hosted by Ondřej Holzman and Luboš Kreč, interviewing figures shaping Czech business and markets. Long-form interview format regularly surfaces founder/investor detail — strategy, valuations, expansion plans — that never appears in written coverage or filings. Observed episodes include algorithmic-trading founders (Martin Schmid / EquiLibre, Petr Zahradník / Qminers) and acquisition financiers (Pavel Drobil / Anacot Capital). Episode pages carry text summaries, so they are machine-readable without audio transcription.

The single best-curated Czech-language fintech archive found in this cell: a working topic page with 101 articles across 4 pages, pagination via ?pi=N. Headlines observed are exactly the target signal type — 'Direct Fidoo ... spouští platformu pro malé a střední podniky' (17.6.2026), Revolut at 1.2m Czech users (24.3.2026), Wflow passing CZK 100m ARR (26.2.2026), and 'Česko má první sandbox pro fintechové startupy, otevřelo ho 21 projektům' (4.2.2026). Lupa is published in the Internet Info stable (shares the /do-mailu/ newsletter infrastructure with Měšec.cz), and is editorially serious about telecom/IT/fintech infrastructure.

127 articles across 5 pages, and the densest pure-payments Czech-language stream located in this cell. Observed headlines cover exactly the A1-adjacent weak signals: Apple leading Czech digital-subscription payments (31.7.2026), 'Fidoo z Directu chce být vrstvou nad bankami' (17.6.2026), Mastercard + ČSOB testing AI-driven shopping in Czechia (6.5.2026), Huawei watches gaining contactless (13.4.2026), and a DDoS attack on the PayU payment gateway (2.4.2026). Covers gateways, acquirers, wallets and bank-scheme partnerships — the merchant-integration layer that regulated disclosures never describe.

34 articles; smaller than the payments archive but distinctly focused on bank-side technology, fraud and channel innovation. Observed items include Komerční banka reporting rising cyber-fraud losses (22.4.2026), a Czech surge in authorised-push-payment style phone fraud (2.2.2026), Revolut launching in-app caller verification against bank-impersonation fraud (13.1.2026), Česká spořitelna opening an AI/VR-equipped nonstop branch (12.11.2025), and quarterly bank cyber-attack volumes (5.5.2025). Useful for tracking bank technology strategy and fraud-driven product launches.

A machine-readable RSS 2.0 feed (MRSS namespace, 20 items, author attribution, enclosure images, persistent GUIDs) confirmed live and current to 25.8.2026. This is the cheapest, most robust ingestion path for the whole Lupa corpus and removes any need to scrape topic pages for ongoing monitoring. Its existence also implies analogous /rss/ endpoints across the Internet Info network (Měšec.cz, Podnikatel.cz), which is worth probing.

Interview podcast running since mid-2018 with e-commerce, IT and media figures. Fintech-relevant episodes exist but are a minority — the most on-point observed was Jan Blažek of Bankovní identita on the European digital identity wallet (29.11.2024), which is directly load-bearing for Czech payments/authentication infrastructure. Each episode has a full article page with a text write-up, so it is text-collectable.

Forbes CZ is explicitly named in this coverage cell. The /tag/fintech/ path resolved and returned a page header reading 'Fintech ▶ ... s Forbes Česko | Forbes', confirming a fintech tag exists and that the tag URL pattern is /tag/<slug>/. Forbes CZ specialises in founder/investor profiles and rich-list style wealth reporting, which names the people and capital behind young Czech payments companies. NOTE: the site renders its article lists client-side — three separate fetches (homepage, /technologie/, /tag/fintech/) each returned only a header line and no article list, so the tag's contents are unverified.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace — Studie českého fintechu (sector study)
why_relevant: A recurring sector study quantifying Czech fintech employment and economic contribution — the project page cites 6,394 people employed including 1,603 foreigners, and public-revenue contribution figures. A companion CzechTrade export brochure (https://czechfintech.cz/project/10647/) describes Czech fintech as a sector with 'more than 200 active firms'. Together these give a defensible denominator for the sector and a second, larger company list beyond the 80+ members.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace — tiskové zprávy (press releases)
why_relevant: First-party press releases from the sector body — the association speaking in its own voice on policy and governance. Confirmed items include the EET/voluntary-sales-record digitalisation position (11.5.2022) and the leadership change putting Miroslav Lukeš and Ondřej Machač at the head of the association (10.3.2022). Useful for tracking who speaks for Czech fintech and what the sector is lobbying for. Note: the two items I could confirm are both from 2022, so publication cadence on this specific category page looks low.

source_name: E15.cz — byznys sections (startupy, finance a bankovnictví, technologie a média)
why_relevant: E15 is a mainstream Czech business daily with a confirmed sub-rubric structure under /byznys/ that maps cleanly onto this cell: /startupy, /finance-a-bankovnictvi, /technologie-a-media, /obchod-a-sluzby. It also runs a consumer-finance vertical (/finexpert/, with /banky-ucty). The startup rubric plus the banking rubric together catch both the funding-round side and the incumbent-bank side of a payments partnership story. An RSS endpoint at /rss and podcasts at /podcasty/ were both confirmed present.

HN (publisher: Economia, a.s.) runs a subdomain-per-rubric structure with tech.hn.cz, byznys.hn.cz and investice.hn.cz all confirmed. It is the most reportorially resourced Czech business title, so it is where a bank-fintech partnership gets investigated rather than announced. A central RSS hub exists at https://rss.hn.cz/, a podcast hub at https://podcasty.hn.cz/ (including the money/investing show MoneyPenny and Krypto Insider), and named newsletters include 'Byznys' (weekly) and 'Peníze' (investment focus).

Czech business/economics portal with Finance, Investování, Technologie and Telekomunikace categories, an open RSS feed at https://www.peak.cz/feed/ and no observed paywall — which makes it unusually cheap to ingest relative to HN or E15. Its fintech/startup focus is thinner than CzechCrunch's, so treat it as breadth coverage and corroboration rather than a primary weak-signal channel. Category URLs follow /category/<topic>/ and author pages /authors/<name>/.

Consumer-finance portal in the Internet Info stable (shares Lupa's /do-mailu/ newsletter infrastructure). Confirmed product-level sections for personal accounts, business accounts, charge cards and credit cards for both consumers and businesses (/produkty/charge-karty/, /produkty/kreditni-karty-pro-podnikatele/). Its value in this cell is different from the tech media: it tracks fee schedules, card product terms and account features at a granularity that reveals competitive moves before any press release does. No paywall observed.

Seznam Zprávy, a.s. (Seznam.cz group) is one of the largest-reach Czech news operations, with a confirmed section pattern /sekce/ekonomika-byznys-216 and article pattern /clanek/ekonomika-byznys-<slug>-<ID>. A separate Tech parent category exists. Reach matters here: a payments story that breaks on Seznam Zprávy sets the national narrative even when CzechCrunch had it first. No paywall was evident on the business magazine section. Note that the observed headline sample was consumer-magazine-ish rather than fintech, so treat fintech density as low.

Official state startup-ecosystem platform under CzechInvest (the old czechstartups.org now 301-redirects here). It exposes structured directories — startups at /startup-ekosystem/startupy/, investors at /startup-ekosystem/investori/, ecosystem data at /startup-data/ and support programmes at /programy/ — and advertises 44 investors, 208 startup infrastructures and 300 events per year. As a pointer this is the state-sanctioned counterpart to the association member list: it names the investors whose portfolio announcements the media in this cell will report.

Satisfies the English-language leg of this cell. Confirmed live tag page carrying Czech funding-round coverage — Sloneek's EUR 3.6m round, ZAKA's EUR 15m Fund I, Elin.ai's EUR 1m pre-seed, Rohlik's EUR 100m unicorn round, Canva's acquisition of Smartmockups — plus an explicit piece on the Czech VC market 'getting more professional'. Deal sizes are given in EUR, which makes cross-country normalisation easy, and English coverage is what international investors and acquirers actually read.

source_name: The Recursive — Czech Republic and fintech tags
why_relevant: CEE-focused English-language tech media ('Meet the world's next tech leaders before anyone else'), with confirmed dedicated tags for Czech Republic (/tag/czech-republic/) and fintech (/tag/fintech/), country tags across the region for comparison, a reports hub at /reports/ and a weekly CEE roundup at /tag/cee-startup-amp-tech-weekly/. The cross-tag intersection (Czech Republic x fintech) is the precise slice this cell needs in English, and the regional framing lets Czech payments developments be benchmarked against Poland and Romania.

Czech investment-focused outlet, a plausible channel for coverage of listed Czech financial institutions, fund flows and fintech investment commentary — i.e. the investor-relations and earnings topics in this run's scope. Unverified: the fetch was refused before any content was returned, so nothing about its structure or current output is confirmed.

Czech e-commerce trade media, the natural home for coverage of payment gateways, checkout methods, BNPL and merchant payment integrations — the acceptance-side signal that neither the startup media nor the banking trade press covers well. Unverified: fetch refused with no body returned, so section structure and payments density are unconfirmed and this remains a hypothesis.

One of the largest Czech consumer-technology outlets, a likely carrier of mobile-wallet, contactless and banking-app coverage (the consumer-facing surface of payments innovation). Unverified: fetch refused with no body returned. Included as a hypothesis to re-probe, not as a confirmed source.

source_name: Patria Online – Investiční doporučení a cílové ceny (výzkum)
why_relevant: Central sell-side research hub of Patria Finance (largest broker on the Prague Stock Exchange), publishing consolidated analyst recommendations and target prices. Fetched content directly showed live entries for all three listed Czech-market banks: Komerční banka (Držet, TP 1111 CZK), Moneta Money Bank (Redukovat, TP 175 CZK) and Erste Bank (Držet, TP 2565 CZK), with research attributed to Patria and KBC Securities. This is the single densest interpretation layer over Czech bank disclosures.

source_name: Patria Online – Komerční banka issuer page (doporučení / zprávy / hospodaření)
why_relevant: Per-issuer analyst view for the largest domestically listed Czech bank. Observed live an aggregated 'Průměrná cílová cena' (average target price, 988.37 CZK) plus sibling tabs for Zprávy (news) and Hospodaření (financial performance), i.e. consensus + restated disclosure data in one place. Consensus drift is a leading indicator of what analysts think changed in KB's reporting.

source_name: Patria Online – Moneta Money Bank issuer analyst page
why_relevant: Analyst recommendation and target-price page for Moneta Money Bank, observed live on the Patria research hub with a 'Redukovat' (Reduce) rating and 175 CZK target. Moneta is the purest retail-banking read-across in the CZ listed universe, so broker revisions here track retail margin and fee expectations.

source_name: Patria Online – Erste Bank (Erste Group) issuer analyst page
why_relevant: Analyst page for Erste Group as traded in Prague — the parent of Česká spořitelna, the largest Czech retail bank. Observed live with 'Držet' (Hold) and a 2565 CZK target. Gives Czech-market analyst framing of a group whose primary disclosures are Austrian, which is exactly the interpretation layer this cell exists to capture.

source_name: Patria Online – Zpravodajství: Akcie (equity news wire)
why_relevant: Patria's equity news stream, where broker commentary on Czech bank results, estimate revisions and rating actions is published in Czech. Confirmed live; article URL pattern is /zpravodajstvi/{id}/{slug}.html, which gives stable, enumerable permalinks suitable for an archive that outlives the issuer's own press page.

source_name: Patria Online – Výsledková sezóna / Kalendář ČR (Czech earnings calendar)
why_relevant: Patria runs an explicit 'Výsledková sezóna' block with per-region reporting calendars ('2Q26 KALENDÁŘ ČR', plus USA and EU). An issuer reporting calendar is the scheduling backbone for a disclosure-monitoring workstream: it tells the collector when Czech bank results are due before they land.

Macro and rates analysis section from the same broker. Bank earnings in CZ are dominated by CNB policy rates and credit-cost expectations, so this is the macro half of the analyst narrative that explains revisions to bank forecasts.

source_name: Kurzy.cz – Zprávy: Oficiální sdělení (official corporate announcements archive)
why_relevant: Confirmed live category on the Kurzy.cz news subdomain carrying 'Oficiální sdělení' — corporate/official notices such as shareholder meetings and statutory announcements. This is precisely the mirror-and-archive function the cell rationale calls for: issuer announcements preserved in a searchable third-party archive with stable numeric permalinks that outlive the original issuer page.

Dedicated press-release category confirmed live on Kurzy.cz. Czech banks and financial institutions push releases into this aggregator, and observed articles were attributed to institutions such as Trinity Bank and Česká spořitelna — so it doubles as a low-effort sweep for bank press output plus attached analyst commentary.

source_name: Kurzy.cz – Akcie ČR / Burza (Prague exchange quote & issuer pages)
why_relevant: Long-running Czech financial portal (operated by Kurzy.cz spol. s r.o. / AliaWeb) with per-issuer quote and exchange pages for the Prague Stock Exchange. Named in the cell brief as a core aggregator; valuable mainly as a durable secondary index of Czech listed banks. Note: per-issuer pages were not reachable by plain fetch (content appears JS-rendered), so the exact per-bank URLs remain unresolved.

source_name: Akcie.cz – analyst notes with target prices (Fio-affiliated portal)
why_relevant: Confirmed live and actively carrying dated analyst notes with explicit Czech-language rating and target-price changes — observed a Komerční banka note with a 1043 CZK target and 'accumulate' rating, plus ČEZ and Colt CZ rating changes, alongside live KB/ERSTE/MONETA quotes. Data credited to BCPP and RM-SYSTÉM, with FIOFONDY / E-BROKER / RM-SYSTÉM branding indicating Fio banka affiliation — i.e. a second, independent Czech broker's view distinct from Patria/KBC.

source_name: Akcie.cz – Novinky z trhu / Zprávy feed
why_relevant: The rolling market-news feed behind Akcie.cz. Confirmed live with a dense, high-frequency stream (sequential article IDs observed in the 219xxx range) covering FX, commodities and macro prints. Sequential IDs make full historical backfill and gap-detection straightforward, which is what makes it useful as an archive layer rather than just a feed.

source_name: Moody's Ratings – public issuer ratings & rating action press releases
why_relevant: Primary publisher of rating actions on Czech banks. Rating action press releases are the highest-signal third-party interrogation of a bank's disclosures: they state explicitly what changed in asset quality, capital or sovereign support assumptions and why. Regulatory rules require the rating and its rationale to be publicly disclosed, so a free tier exists even though the portal is heavily bot-defended.

source_name: S&P Global Ratings – rating actions and research
why_relevant: Second of the big three agencies covering Czech banks and the Czech sovereign. Publishes rating actions, outlook changes and sector commentary (e.g. banking industry country risk assessments) that restate and stress-test issuer disclosures. Sovereign-to-bank rating linkage makes its Czech sovereign actions directly predictive of bank rating moves.

source_name: Fitch Ratings – Czech bank rating actions and criteria commentary
why_relevant: Third of the big three and an active rater of CEE banking groups. Fitch publishes free rating action commentaries (RACs) with unusually explicit reasoning on Viability Ratings and Government Support Ratings, which is the most analytically useful public restatement of a bank's own disclosures.

source_name: WOOD & Company – Insights (public analyses and press releases)
why_relevant: WOOD & Company is the leading independent CEE-focused broker (35+ years, Prague-headquartered) and one of the few houses producing genuine sell-side equity research on CEE banks. The public /insights/ section carries analyses, interviews and press releases — the freely collectible slice of an otherwise gated research franchise.

source_name: WOOD & Company – research portal (gated equity research)
why_relevant: The actual WOOD research distribution portal, surfaced as a link from wood.com. This is where full broker notes on CEE/Czech banks — target prices, estimate tables, sector notes — would live. Worth registering an access route for: it is the highest-quality broker-note source identified in this cell, and no public substitute carries the same depth.

source_name: J&T Banka – Insight / investment commentary and Wealth Report
why_relevant: J&T Banka is a significant Czech investment bank whose analysts are routinely quoted on Czech bank results and the domestic capital market. Confirmed live with an 'Insight' section and a separate Wealth Report property. A useful third independent Czech house alongside Patria/KBC and Fio, though the research section's exact URLs were not resolvable from the homepage fetch.
